questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.1: Analyze workloads to determine monitoring requirements.
questions.text: A payment API handles cardholder-adjacent metadata and is exposed through API Gateway and Lambda. The security team needs near-real-time detection of suspicious access patterns and failed authorization. Which monitoring requirement should be prioritized?

answers.text: Capture API access logs, Lambda application errors, authentication outcomes, and security findings with alerting on abnormal patterns
Collect only monthly cost reports for the API account
Rely only on Lambda deployment package checksums
Monitor only successful HTTP 200 responses

explanations.a: The workload includes an internet-facing API and sensitive transaction context, so monitoring must cover request activity, application failures, authentication behavior, and security findings together.
explanations.b: Cost reports can support financial review, but monitoring requirements for a payment API need operational and security signals.
explanations.c: Package integrity is useful, but it does not reveal suspicious access patterns or failed authorization at runtime.
explanations.d: Successful responses alone miss failed authorization, suspicious request rates, and backend errors.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.1: Analyze workloads to determine monitoring requirements.
questions.text: A batch analytics workload runs once per night in a private subnet and reads encrypted S3 data. The business asks for security monitoring without high-volume debug logs. Which approach fits the workload?

answers.text: Enable verbose application debug logging forever for every record processed
Monitor job success, data access events for sensitive buckets, key access, and exception logs with targeted retention
Monitor only public web request metrics
Disable all data access logging because the subnet is private

explanations.a: Full debug retention can create excessive sensitive data exposure and cost for a nightly batch workload.
explanations.b: The workload is scheduled and data-sensitive, so monitoring should focus on execution outcome, protected data access, KMS usage, and meaningful failures rather than continuous debug noise.
explanations.c: The workload is private and batch-oriented, so web request metrics do not cover the main security and execution risks.
explanations.d: Private networking does not remove the need to monitor access to sensitive S3 and KMS resources.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.1: Analyze workloads to determine monitoring requirements.
questions.text: A multi-account organization has workloads with different criticality. The security team wants to set alert thresholds. What should drive the monitoring requirements?

answers.text: The alphabetical order of account names
The number of dashboards a team already has
Workload risk, data sensitivity, exposure, recovery objectives, and ownership model
A single identical threshold for every resource type in every account

explanations.a: Account naming order does not represent business impact or security exposure.
explanations.b: Existing dashboard count does not define required detection coverage.
explanations.c: Monitoring requirements should reflect business impact and threat exposure so alerting is aligned to the actual risk of each workload.
explanations.d: Uniform thresholds can over-alert low-risk workloads and miss important signals in critical workloads.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.1: Analyze workloads to determine monitoring requirements.
questions.text: A public application uses CloudFront, AWS WAF, and an ALB. The team needs to detect credential stuffing and layer 7 attacks. Which monitoring signals matter most?

answers.text: Only EBS volume throughput on backend instances
Only CloudFormation stack output values
Only successful deployment events from the pipeline
AWS WAF logs, CloudFront access logs, ALB request metrics, and authentication failure patterns

explanations.a: Storage throughput can support performance analysis but does not detect web-layer attack behavior.
explanations.b: Stack outputs expose deployment values and do not show active attack traffic.
explanations.c: Deployment events do not reveal credential stuffing or web-layer request patterns.
explanations.d: Credential stuffing and layer 7 attacks are visible through edge, web firewall, load balancer, and identity-related request patterns.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.1: Analyze workloads to determine monitoring requirements.
questions.text: A workload processes confidential documents and stores them in S3. The team must detect accidental exposure and sensitive data placement. What monitoring requirement is most relevant?

answers.text: Monitor S3 public access changes, object-level activity where required, and Amazon Macie findings
Track only CPU utilization of unrelated EC2 instances
Use only Route 53 health checks for the bucket name
Monitor only container image vulnerability scans

explanations.a: Confidential document monitoring should include exposure detection, object access visibility, and sensitive data discovery.
explanations.b: CPU utilization does not reveal S3 exposure or sensitive document classification.
explanations.c: Health checks do not classify or audit objects in S3.
explanations.d: Image scanning does not detect sensitive data exposure in S3 objects.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.1: Analyze workloads to determine monitoring requirements.
questions.text: A security operations team is onboarding a new workload. Which question best helps define detection requirements?

answers.text: Which dashboard color does the application team prefer?
Which assets, identities, data, entry points, and failure modes are most important to protect?
How many unused subnets exist in the account?
Which service has the shortest name in the architecture?

explanations.a: Dashboard styling does not determine detection coverage.
explanations.b: Detection design starts by identifying what matters, how it can be accessed, and which failure or attack paths must be visible.
explanations.c: Unused subnet count might support hygiene review but does not define the workload's key detection needs.
explanations.d: Service name length has no security monitoring relevance.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.1: Analyze workloads to determine monitoring requirements.
questions.text: A workload uses generative AI features through Amazon Bedrock and stores prompts and outputs. The security team must monitor for abuse while limiting sensitive logging. What is the best monitoring requirement?

answers.text: Log every prompt and response in plaintext forever
Monitor only EC2 disk metrics because AI workloads always run on instances
Capture policy-relevant invocation metadata, guardrail outcomes, access events, and redacted application logs
Ignore model access events if the application has authentication

explanations.a: Full plaintext retention can expose sensitive data and may violate data minimization requirements.
explanations.b: Bedrock usage and guardrail behavior are service-level signals, not simply EC2 disk activity.
explanations.c: Generative AI monitoring should include who invoked the model, which controls acted, and safe diagnostic context without storing unnecessary sensitive prompt content.
explanations.d: Authentication does not remove the need to monitor model usage and abuse indicators.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.2: Design and implement workload monitoring strategies.
questions.text: A company wants to know if its primary website is reachable from outside AWS and if users receive 5XX errors. Which workload monitoring strategy fits?

answers.text: Monitor only instance memory with no endpoint checks
Review access logs manually once a month
Use CloudTrail management events as the only website health signal
Use synthetic health checks or canaries with CloudWatch metrics and alarms on availability and error rates

explanations.a: Memory metrics can help diagnosis but do not prove the public website is reachable.
explanations.b: Monthly manual review is too slow for availability monitoring.
explanations.c: CloudTrail records control-plane calls and does not measure live website availability.
explanations.d: External health checks and error-rate alarms validate the user-facing path rather than only internal component status.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.2: Design and implement workload monitoring strategies.
questions.text: A Lambda-based API has intermittent downstream timeouts. What monitoring strategy should be implemented?

answers.text: Track Lambda errors, duration, throttles, downstream dependency latency, and correlation IDs
Track only the count of Lambda function versions
Use only S3 bucket access logs for the deployment package
Disable logs to reduce noise during timeout periods

explanations.a: Timeout diagnosis requires function health, dependency timing, and request correlation across the path.
explanations.b: Version count does not reveal runtime timeout behavior.
explanations.c: Deployment package access does not show function execution or dependency latency.
explanations.d: Removing logs makes intermittent timeout investigation harder.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.2: Design and implement workload monitoring strategies.
questions.text: A VPC workload has strict egress requirements. The team wants monitoring for unexpected outbound connections. Which strategy is appropriate?

answers.text: Monitor only AWS Billing console logins
Collect VPC Flow Logs and inspect egress patterns with alerts for unauthorized destinations
Collect only application feature flag changes
Rely only on subnet names that include private

explanations.a: Billing logins do not show network egress behavior.
explanations.b: Flow logs provide network metadata that can reveal unexpected outbound paths and destinations.
explanations.c: Feature flag events do not identify outbound network destinations.
explanations.d: Subnet names do not prove egress is restricted or monitored.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.2: Design and implement workload monitoring strategies.
questions.text: A containerized service on Amazon EKS must detect pod crashes, unauthorized image changes, and suspicious runtime behavior. Which monitoring strategy is strongest?

answers.text: Use only Route 53 Resolver query logs
Track only the cluster creation date
Combine Kubernetes workload metrics, container logs, image scanning, and GuardDuty runtime or EKS-related findings
Disable container logs after deployment

explanations.a: DNS query logs can help some investigations but do not show pod crashes or image vulnerability status.
explanations.b: Creation date does not reveal runtime security or stability issues.
explanations.c: EKS security monitoring needs workload health, image integrity signals, and threat findings that cover runtime behavior.
explanations.d: Container logs are needed to diagnose crashes and suspicious behavior.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.2: Design and implement workload monitoring strategies.
questions.text: A workload uses an SQS queue and consumers. Messages sometimes age for too long without errors. What should be monitored?

answers.text: Only the queue name length
Only IAM user password age
Only CloudFront cache hit ratio
ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage, queue depth, consumer errors, and consumer processing duration

explanations.a: Queue name length has no operational or security meaning.
explanations.b: Password age does not measure queue processing delay.
explanations.c: Cache hit ratio does not reveal SQS backlog or consumer failure.
explanations.d: Queue age and consumer health indicate whether asynchronous processing is keeping up.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.2: Design and implement workload monitoring strategies.
questions.text: A security monitoring plan includes AWS Config conformance packs for baseline controls. What workload strategy does this support?

answers.text: Continuous evaluation of resource configuration against security requirements
Real-time packet capture for every VPC packet
Replacement of application logging
Automatic proof that every application request is authorized

explanations.a: Conformance packs group Config rules so workloads can be assessed against expected security posture.
explanations.b: Config evaluates resource configuration; it does not provide packet-level capture.
explanations.c: Configuration compliance does not replace application and service logs.
explanations.d: Config rules evaluate resources and cannot prove every runtime authorization decision.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.2: Design and implement workload monitoring strategies.
questions.text: A team monitors a critical API with dashboards but no alarms. What is the main weakness?

answers.text: Dashboards cannot display CloudWatch metrics
Dashboards depend on someone looking at them and do not notify responders automatically
Alarms are useful only for cost metrics
A dashboard automatically remediates every incident

explanations.a: Dashboards can display CloudWatch metrics, but they do not page by themselves.
explanations.b: Monitoring strategies for critical workloads need alerting paths, not only passive visualization.
explanations.c: Alarms can evaluate operational, security, and custom metrics.
explanations.d: Dashboards provide visibility and do not perform response actions by default.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.3: Aggregate security and monitoring events.
questions.text: A security operations team needs one place to view findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and AWS Config across accounts. Which service should aggregate these findings?

answers.text: Amazon CloudFront
AWS CodeArtifact
AWS Security Hub
Amazon EFS

explanations.a: CloudFront delivers content and does not aggregate security findings.
explanations.b: CodeArtifact stores packages and does not centralize security events.
explanations.c: Security Hub aggregates and normalizes findings from supported AWS security services across accounts and Regions.
explanations.d: EFS provides file storage and does not aggregate monitoring findings.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.3: Aggregate security and monitoring events.
questions.text: An organization wants to centralize security-related logs in OCSF format for analytics and third-party tool integration. Which service is most aligned?

answers.text: AWS Backup
AWS Certificate Manager
Amazon Cognito user pools only
Amazon Security Lake

explanations.a: Backup stores recovery points and does not normalize security telemetry for analytics.
explanations.b: ACM manages certificates and does not aggregate OCSF security logs.
explanations.c: Cognito can emit identity-related logs, but it is not the organization-wide security data lake.
explanations.d: Security Lake centralizes security data in a security data lake and normalizes supported sources into OCSF.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.3: Aggregate security and monitoring events.
questions.text: A multi-account organization wants GuardDuty findings from every account to be managed by a security account. What should be configured?

answers.text: GuardDuty delegated administrator with member account management
Separate standalone GuardDuty administrators in every workload account
A public S3 bucket where every account writes findings manually
Only CloudWatch dashboards in the management account

explanations.a: Delegated administration centralizes GuardDuty configuration and findings across the organization.
explanations.b: Standalone administration fragments visibility and makes consistent response harder.
explanations.c: Public manual aggregation is insecure and unreliable.
explanations.d: Dashboards alone do not delegate or aggregate GuardDuty administration.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.3: Aggregate security and monitoring events.
questions.text: A company aggregates events from AWS accounts into a SIEM. What design improves event ownership and routing?

answers.text: Strip all source account and resource identifiers
Include account, Region, resource, severity, service, and finding identifiers in the event pipeline
Replace severity with random numeric values
Store all events as unsearchable images

explanations.a: Removing source context makes investigations and ownership assignment harder.
explanations.b: Consistent event metadata lets responders filter, route, deduplicate, and correlate security activity.
explanations.c: Random severity breaks prioritization and escalation.
explanations.d: Image-only storage prevents efficient querying and correlation.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.3: Aggregate security and monitoring events.
questions.text: A team wants to combine CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and Route 53 Resolver query logs for threat hunting. What capability is needed?

answers.text: Separate local files on each instance with no central query
A single alarm that triggers only on CPU utilization
A central analytics store that preserves source fields and supports query correlation
A manual spreadsheet of suspicious IPs with no event ingestion

explanations.a: Local-only files prevent cross-source correlation at scale.
explanations.b: CPU alarms do not aggregate control-plane, network, and DNS evidence.
explanations.c: Threat hunting across control-plane, network, and DNS sources requires searchable fields and time correlation.
explanations.d: Static spreadsheets do not provide continuous event aggregation.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.3: Aggregate security and monitoring events.
questions.text: A company uses AWS Organizations and wants to aggregate monitoring events without using the management account for daily security operations. Which pattern fits?

answers.text: Run all production workloads in the management account
Share the management account root user with every security analyst
Disable organization integration and rely on email exports
Use delegated administrator accounts for supported security services

explanations.a: Workloads in the management account increase blast radius and are not needed for security aggregation.
explanations.b: Shared root access removes accountability and creates organization-wide risk.
explanations.c: Email exports are delayed and do not provide scalable aggregation.
explanations.d: Delegated administrator accounts centralize service operations while reducing routine use of the management account.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.3: Aggregate security and monitoring events.
questions.text: Security Hub receives duplicate findings from multiple sources for the same exposed S3 bucket. What should the response process do?

answers.text: Correlate and deduplicate by resource, finding type, and time while preserving source evidence
Delete all but one source service permanently
Treat every duplicate as a separate unrelated incident
Ignore the exposed bucket because duplicates exist

explanations.a: Deduplication reduces noise, and source evidence remains useful for validation and audit.
explanations.b: Removing detection sources can create blind spots.
explanations.c: Duplicate findings for the same resource can create response noise.
explanations.d: Duplicate findings do not reduce the severity of the underlying exposure.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.4: Create metrics, alerts, and dashboards to detect anomalous data and events.
questions.text: A company wants to detect unusual API call patterns in AWS accounts without writing custom rules for every API. Which service should be enabled?

answers.text: AWS CodeDeploy
Amazon GuardDuty
Amazon EFS Lifecycle policies
AWS DataSync

explanations.a: CodeDeploy manages application deployments and does not provide managed threat detection.
explanations.b: GuardDuty analyzes AWS activity and other signals to detect anomalous or suspicious behavior.
explanations.c: EFS lifecycle policies manage file storage classes and not API anomaly detection.
explanations.d: DataSync moves data and does not detect anomalous API behavior.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.4: Create metrics, alerts, and dashboards to detect anomalous data and events.
questions.text: A security dashboard must show open critical Inspector findings, GuardDuty finding counts, and Macie sensitive data findings by account. What should the dashboard use?

answers.text: Only Lambda memory size by function
Only S3 request count for public assets
Aggregated findings from Security Hub or source services with account and severity dimensions
Only CloudFormation template descriptions

explanations.a: Lambda memory size does not summarize security findings across services.
explanations.b: Request count can show activity but not vulnerability, threat, and sensitive-data findings.
explanations.c: Security dashboards need normalized finding data and dimensions that support account-level risk views.
explanations.d: Template descriptions do not provide live security findings.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.4: Create metrics, alerts, and dashboards to detect anomalous data and events.
questions.text: A team wants an alert when an S3 bucket policy becomes public. Which signal is most appropriate?

answers.text: An ALB target response time alarm
A DynamoDB consumed capacity alarm
A CodeBuild queued build alarm
AWS Config or Security Hub finding with an EventBridge rule for notification

explanations.a: ALB latency does not detect S3 bucket policy exposure.
explanations.b: DynamoDB capacity does not detect S3 public access.
explanations.c: Build queue duration does not detect bucket policy risk.
explanations.d: Config and Security Hub can evaluate public access posture and emit events that can trigger response.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.4: Create metrics, alerts, and dashboards to detect anomalous data and events.
questions.text: A workload has normal traffic spikes during business hours but a rare spike in denied requests at midnight. What helps detect this anomaly?

answers.text: CloudWatch anomaly detection or metric alarms based on historical patterns
A fixed threshold that ignores normal daily patterns
A manual check of logs every quarter
Disabling denied request logging

explanations.a: Anomaly-aware metrics can identify unusual behavior relative to expected time-based patterns.
explanations.b: Static thresholds can miss unusual off-hour behavior or create daytime false positives.
explanations.c: Quarterly review is too slow for anomalous request detection.
explanations.d: Removing denied request signals prevents anomaly detection.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.4: Create metrics, alerts, and dashboards to detect anomalous data and events.
questions.text: A security team wants recurring evidence that all accounts meet baseline controls. Which automation should create regular assessments?

answers.text: One handwritten checklist per account stored locally
AWS Config conformance packs with scheduled evaluation and aggregated compliance reporting
CloudFront cache invalidation after every assessment
ECR tag mutation for every account

explanations.a: Manual local checklists are not continuous or centrally aggregated.
explanations.b: Conformance packs can continuously assess baseline controls and provide aggregated compliance status.
explanations.c: Cache invalidation does not assess security baselines.
explanations.d: Image tag changes do not evaluate account security controls.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.4: Create metrics, alerts, and dashboards to detect anomalous data and events.
questions.text: A team wants to investigate anomalous GuardDuty findings quickly from a dashboard. What should the dashboard link or expose?

answers.text: Only a total count with no links or resource identity
Only the company logo and environment names
Finding details, affected resources, account, Region, severity, and investigation runbook
Only unrelated cost forecasts

explanations.a: A count alone slows triage because responders cannot identify scope or next steps.
explanations.b: Branding and labels do not provide investigation detail.
explanations.c: Actionable dashboards provide context and a response path, not only a raw count.
explanations.d: Cost forecasts do not explain active security findings.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.4: Create metrics, alerts, and dashboards to detect anomalous data and events.
questions.text: A Macie job discovers sensitive data in a bucket that should contain only public assets. What alerting design is appropriate?

answers.text: Alert only the web performance team with no bucket context
Suppress all Macie findings from public asset accounts
Publish the detected sensitive content in the alert body
Notify the data owner and security team with bucket, object classification, severity, and remediation guidance

explanations.a: Performance owners may not be the data owner, and missing bucket context delays response.
explanations.b: Suppressing findings can hide accidental sensitive data placement.
explanations.c: Alerts should avoid spreading sensitive content further.
explanations.d: Sensitive data findings require clear ownership, classification context, and a path to remove or protect the data.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.4: Create metrics, alerts, and dashboards to detect anomalous data and events.
questions.text: A dashboard for security leadership should not expose raw logs but should show posture trends. What should it include?

answers.text: Aggregated trend metrics for findings, compliance status, remediation age, and coverage gaps
Full request bodies from every application log
Only detailed stack traces from production
Only the names of enabled Regions

explanations.a: Leadership dashboards should summarize risk posture and improvement trends without exposing unnecessary sensitive event details.
explanations.b: Raw request bodies can contain sensitive data and are not suitable for a leadership summary.
explanations.c: Stack traces are too granular and can expose internals.
explanations.d: Region names alone do not show detection coverage or risk trend.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.5: Create and manage automations to perform regular assessments and investigations.
questions.text: A security team wants regular checks that all member accounts have CloudTrail enabled and S3 Block Public Access configured. Which automation fits?

answers.text: A developer reminder to inspect accounts manually
AWS Config conformance pack deployed across accounts
A CloudFront distribution with access logs
An EBS snapshot lifecycle policy

explanations.a: Manual reminders do not provide continuous assessment or central reporting.
explanations.b: Conformance packs can evaluate multiple security controls consistently across accounts.
explanations.c: CloudFront logging does not evaluate account baseline controls.
explanations.d: Snapshot lifecycle does not assess CloudTrail or S3 public access settings.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.5: Create and manage automations to perform regular assessments and investigations.
questions.text: A team wants to automatically investigate GuardDuty findings by collecting related CloudTrail activity and resource metadata. Which orchestration pattern fits?

answers.text: A weekly manual export of findings to a spreadsheet
A Route 53 failover record for the finding ID
EventBridge rule that invokes a Step Functions or Lambda investigation workflow
An S3 lifecycle expiration rule on the evidence bucket

explanations.a: Weekly exports delay investigation and lack automated enrichment.
explanations.b: DNS failover does not collect evidence for findings.
explanations.c: Security findings can trigger serverless workflows that gather evidence and enrich the incident record.
explanations.d: Lifecycle expiration manages retention and does not perform investigation.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.5: Create and manage automations to perform regular assessments and investigations.
questions.text: A company needs recurring vulnerability assessments for container images and Lambda functions. Which service should be included?

answers.text: AWS Certificate Manager
Amazon Route 53 Resolver only
AWS DataSync
Amazon Inspector

explanations.a: ACM manages TLS certificates and does not scan images or Lambda functions for vulnerabilities.
explanations.b: Resolver handles DNS queries and does not perform vulnerability assessment.
explanations.c: DataSync transfers data and does not scan compute artifacts.
explanations.d: Inspector assesses supported workloads and container images for vulnerabilities.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.5: Create and manage automations to perform regular assessments and investigations.
questions.text: A compliance team requires automatic remediation when a security group allows unrestricted SSH. What design is appropriate?

answers.text: AWS Config rule detection with Systems Manager Automation or Lambda remediation
A dashboard note that says SSH is not allowed
Manual review once per year
A metric alarm on unrelated CPU utilization

explanations.a: Config can detect noncompliant security group rules and automation can apply approved remediation.
explanations.b: A note provides awareness but does not detect or remediate drift.
explanations.c: Annual review leaves a long exposure window.
explanations.d: CPU utilization does not detect unrestricted SSH rules.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.5: Create and manage automations to perform regular assessments and investigations.
questions.text: A security operations team wants daily assessment of accounts for Trusted Advisor and Security Hub posture. What is most important?

answers.text: Only ad hoc screenshots from one account
Automated collection with consistent account coverage and exception tracking
No exception records because exceptions are temporary
Only a random sample of low-risk accounts

explanations.a: Screenshots do not provide consistent organization-wide coverage.
explanations.b: Regular assessments need complete coverage and a way to distinguish accepted exceptions from unresolved findings.
explanations.c: Accepted exceptions still need owner, scope, and expiration.
explanations.d: Sampling can miss high-risk or newly created accounts.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.5: Create and manage automations to perform regular assessments and investigations.
questions.text: A new account is created in AWS Organizations. Security baselines should be assessed immediately. What automation trigger should be used?

answers.text: Wait for the first production incident in the account
Use only a monthly calendar reminder with no account discovery
Account creation or Control Tower lifecycle events that start baseline assessment
Require the account owner to email screenshots

explanations.a: Incident-triggered assessment leaves the account unverified until after potential impact.
explanations.b: Calendar reminders can miss new accounts or delay assessment.
explanations.c: Lifecycle events allow the organization to assess and configure new accounts as soon as they are onboarded.
explanations.d: Email screenshots are not reliable assessment automation.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.1.5: Create and manage automations to perform regular assessments and investigations.
questions.text: A security automation frequently remediates the same noncompliant resource, but the owner reverts it manually. What should be added?

answers.text: Increase remediation frequency without contacting the owner
Suppress the finding permanently without review
Delete all monitoring for that resource
Investigation of the root cause and owner notification with policy enforcement or exception workflow

explanations.a: More frequent changes do not solve conflicting ownership behavior.
explanations.b: Suppression can hide a real policy violation.
explanations.c: Removing detection worsens governance and compliance visibility.
explanations.d: Repeated remediation indicates a process or ownership issue that needs escalation, governance, or a documented exception.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.1: Identify sources for log ingestion and storage based on requirements.
questions.text: A regulated workload needs logs for API calls, VPC traffic, DNS queries, and application errors. Which log source set is most appropriate?

answers.text: CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, Route 53 Resolver query logs, and application logs
Only application standard output
Only CloudFront access logs
Only ECR scan results

explanations.a: The requirements span control-plane activity, network traffic metadata, DNS lookups, and application behavior.
explanations.b: Application logs do not capture all AWS API calls, VPC flows, or DNS queries.
explanations.c: CloudFront logs edge requests but do not cover VPC flows or all control-plane activity.
explanations.d: Image scan results do not provide runtime API, network, DNS, and application logs.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.1: Identify sources for log ingestion and storage based on requirements.
questions.text: A company must audit S3 object reads for a sensitive bucket. Which log source should be selected?

answers.text: CloudTrail management events only
CloudTrail data events for the specific S3 bucket
VPC Flow Logs only
AWS Config snapshots only

explanations.a: Management events do not include every object read and write operation.
explanations.b: S3 data events record object-level API activity when enabled for the bucket.
explanations.c: Flow logs show network metadata and do not identify S3 object API names and keys.
explanations.d: Config records resource configuration and not every object read operation.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.1: Identify sources for log ingestion and storage based on requirements.
questions.text: An application communicates with suspicious domains from private subnets. Which logs help investigate the domain lookups?

answers.text: CloudFormation stack outputs
EBS volume performance metrics
Route 53 Resolver query logs
IAM credential reports

explanations.a: Stack outputs expose deployment values and do not show DNS query activity.
explanations.b: Volume metrics do not reveal queried domains.
explanations.c: Resolver query logs capture DNS queries from VPC resources that use Route 53 Resolver.
explanations.d: Credential reports describe IAM users and do not show DNS lookups.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.1: Identify sources for log ingestion and storage based on requirements.
questions.text: A hybrid network uses AWS Transit Gateway and the security team needs traffic metadata between attached networks. Which source should be considered?

answers.text: S3 server access logs for a static bucket
Lambda function concurrency metrics
CloudWatch dashboard annotations only
Transit gateway flow logs

explanations.a: S3 access logs do not show transit gateway network flows.
explanations.b: Concurrency metrics do not describe hybrid network traffic.
explanations.c: Annotations provide context but do not ingest network flow data.
explanations.d: Transit gateway flow logs provide network flow metadata for traffic through the transit gateway.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.1: Identify sources for log ingestion and storage based on requirements.
questions.text: A team needs to choose log storage for seven-year retention and Athena queries over security logs. Which storage target is appropriate?

answers.text: Amazon S3 with partitioned log layout, encryption, lifecycle, and access controls
Only ephemeral instance store on a logging instance
Only CloudWatch Logs with one-day retention
Only a developer laptop with compressed log files

explanations.a: S3 supports durable long-term log storage and can be queried by Athena when data is organized and cataloged.
explanations.b: Instance store is not durable long-term log storage.
explanations.c: One-day retention conflicts with the seven-year requirement.
explanations.d: Laptop storage is not controlled, durable, or centrally queryable.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.1: Identify sources for log ingestion and storage based on requirements.
questions.text: A workload has a privacy requirement to avoid storing full request payloads unless necessary. What should guide log source selection?

answers.text: Always log complete payloads and secrets for every request
Collect the minimum fields required for security analysis and mask or exclude sensitive payload content
Disable all logs because some data is sensitive
Store sensitive logs in public buckets for transparency

explanations.a: Full payload logging can create privacy and credential exposure risk.
explanations.b: Log ingestion should meet detection needs while minimizing unnecessary sensitive data retention.
explanations.c: Sensitive data concerns should drive minimization and masking, not complete loss of security evidence.
explanations.d: Public storage would expose sensitive data and violate access-control expectations.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.1: Identify sources for log ingestion and storage based on requirements.
questions.text: A security tool needs logs from CloudTrail, DNS, VPC traffic, and supported security services in a normalized data lake. Which source and storage approach fits?

answers.text: CloudWatch alarm history only
A single application log file on one EC2 instance
Amazon Security Lake with supported AWS log and finding sources enabled
An IAM policy document stored as a log source

explanations.a: Alarm history does not contain the full normalized set of control-plane, DNS, flow, and security findings.
explanations.b: One instance log file cannot represent organization-wide security telemetry.
explanations.c: Security Lake centralizes and normalizes supported security data so analytics and third-party integrations can consume it.
explanations.d: Policies define permissions and are not a live security log ingestion source.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.2: Configure logging for AWS services and applications.
questions.keyword: AWS service and application logging configuration
questions.text: A company wants CloudTrail enabled for all current and future accounts in AWS Organizations. What should be configured?

answers.text: Separate optional trails created manually by each team
Only application debug logs in each account
Only VPC Flow Logs for public subnets
An organization trail that delivers to a centralized, protected log bucket

explanations.a: Manual per-account trails can be missed or disabled inconsistently.
explanations.b: Application logs do not replace account-level API audit logs.
explanations.c: Flow logs show network metadata and do not capture all management API activity.
explanations.d: An organization trail captures management events across member accounts and centralizes audit log delivery.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.2: Configure logging for AWS services and applications.
questions.keyword: AWS service and application logging configuration
questions.text: An EC2 application writes security events to a local file. The team needs these events in CloudWatch Logs. What should be configured?

answers.text: CloudWatch agent file collection with an instance role that can write logs
CloudTrail data events for the EC2 root volume
An ALB listener rule that points to the log file
A KMS alias named after the log file

explanations.a: The CloudWatch agent needs a file path configuration and permissions to publish events to the target log group.
explanations.b: CloudTrail does not ingest arbitrary application log files from an instance.
explanations.c: Listener rules route HTTP requests and do not ship host log files.
explanations.d: Key aliases do not collect application logs.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.2: Configure logging for AWS services and applications.
questions.keyword: AWS service and application logging configuration
questions.text: API Gateway access logs are missing from a production stage. What configuration should be checked?

answers.text: Only the Lambda function memory setting
Stage access logging settings, destination log group, and required CloudWatch Logs permissions
Only the Route 53 record TTL
Only the S3 lifecycle rule for unrelated artifacts

explanations.a: Function memory does not enable API Gateway stage access logging.
explanations.b: API Gateway needs logging enabled on the stage and permission to write to the configured destination.
explanations.c: DNS TTL does not control API Gateway log delivery.
explanations.d: Artifact lifecycle rules do not configure API Gateway logging.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.2: Configure logging for AWS services and applications.
questions.keyword: AWS service and application logging configuration
questions.text: A CloudFront distribution should send standard access logs to a storage location for analysis. What must be configured?

answers.text: An EC2 instance profile on the viewer's browser
A DynamoDB TTL setting
CloudFront logging destination and permissions for the log delivery target
A Lambda reserved concurrency setting

explanations.a: Viewer browsers do not use EC2 instance profiles for CloudFront logging.
explanations.b: DynamoDB TTL does not enable CloudFront access log delivery.
explanations.c: CloudFront access logging requires an eligible destination and permissions so log files can be delivered.
explanations.d: Lambda concurrency does not configure CloudFront logging.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.2: Configure logging for AWS services and applications.
questions.keyword: AWS service and application logging configuration
questions.text: A Lambda function is not writing logs to CloudWatch Logs after deployment. What should be reviewed?

answers.text: Only the function tag count
Only the S3 bucket policy of an unrelated bucket
Only the CloudFront cache policy
Execution role permissions for logs and application logging behavior

explanations.a: Tags help organization but do not grant log write permission.
explanations.b: An unrelated bucket policy does not authorize CloudWatch Logs writes.
explanations.c: Cache policy does not control Lambda log emission.
explanations.d: Lambda needs permission to create and write log streams, and the function code or runtime must emit log output.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.2: Configure logging for AWS services and applications.
questions.keyword: AWS service and application logging configuration
questions.text: A company wants centralized CloudWatch Logs from multiple accounts in a dedicated logging account. Which design can support this?

answers.text: Cross-account log subscriptions or centralized observability configuration with scoped permissions
Public write access to the logging account for any principal
Manual copy and paste of log events during incidents
A shared root password for the logging account

explanations.a: Centralized logging needs an authorized delivery path from workload accounts to the logging destination.
explanations.b: Public write access can allow log injection and is not a controlled aggregation method.
explanations.c: Manual copying is incomplete and too slow for centralized observability.
explanations.d: Root credential sharing is unsafe and unnecessary for log aggregation.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.2: Configure logging for AWS services and applications.
questions.keyword: AWS service and application logging configuration
questions.text: A team needs to log AWS WAF requests for a CloudFront distribution. What should be configured?

answers.text: Only ALB access logs for an unrelated load balancer
AWS WAF logging to a supported destination with appropriate redaction if required
Only CloudTrail management events
Only EBS volume encryption

explanations.a: Unrelated ALB logs do not show WAF decisions at the CloudFront web ACL.
explanations.b: AWS WAF logging captures inspected web requests and can redact fields that should not be stored.
explanations.c: CloudTrail records WAF configuration changes but not every inspected web request.
explanations.d: Volume encryption does not capture WAF request details.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.2: Configure logging for AWS services and applications.
questions.keyword: AWS service and application logging configuration
questions.text: A security team wants to preserve logs after a workload account compromise. What logging architecture is strongest?

answers.text: Store logs only in the workload account with broad administrator delete access
Store logs only on the compromised instances
Deliver logs to a separate log archive account with restrictive bucket and KMS policies
Disable centralized logging during incidents

explanations.a: Same-account broad access increases the chance of evidence loss during compromise.
explanations.b: Instance-local logs are easy to tamper with or lose.
explanations.c: A separate protected archive reduces the chance that compromised workload administrators can delete or alter audit evidence.
explanations.d: Disabling logging removes evidence when it is most needed.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.3: Implement log storage and log data lakes and integrate with third-party security tools.
questions.keyword: Log storage and security data lake integration
questions.text: A company wants a security log data lake that can be queried and shared with a third-party SIEM. Which service should be evaluated?

answers.text: AWS Certificate Manager
Amazon EFS only
AWS CodeDeploy
Amazon Security Lake

explanations.a: ACM manages certificates and does not operate a security log data lake.
explanations.b: EFS provides file storage and is not a normalized security data lake service.
explanations.c: CodeDeploy manages deployments and does not centralize security telemetry.
explanations.d: Security Lake centralizes supported security logs and findings and makes them available for analytics and integrations.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.3: Implement log storage and log data lakes and integrate with third-party security tools.
questions.keyword: Log storage and security data lake integration
questions.text: A security lake stores logs in S3. What access-control design is important?

answers.text: Use least-privilege access, encryption, and separate roles for ingestion, administration, and analysis
Give every workload administrator delete access to all lake objects
Make the lake bucket public so third-party tools can read it
Use one shared access key for every analyst and tool

explanations.a: A security data lake contains sensitive evidence, so duties and permissions should be separated and encrypted storage enforced.
explanations.b: Broad delete access can compromise evidence retention.
explanations.c: Public access exposes security telemetry and is not a controlled integration.
explanations.d: Shared keys remove accountability and complicate rotation.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.3: Implement log storage and log data lakes and integrate with third-party security tools.
questions.keyword: Log storage and security data lake integration
questions.text: A third-party SIEM expects normalized security events. What pipeline capability helps before ingestion?

answers.text: Remove all timestamps to reduce parsing complexity
Parse and normalize events into a common schema such as OCSF where appropriate
Convert all events into screenshots
Store only the first line of every event

explanations.a: Timestamps are required for correlation and investigation.
explanations.b: Normalization lets tools correlate events from different sources more consistently.
explanations.c: Screenshots cannot be queried or normalized effectively.
explanations.d: Truncating events can remove fields needed for security analysis.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.3: Implement log storage and log data lakes and integrate with third-party security tools.
questions.keyword: Log storage and security data lake integration
questions.text: A log archive must support long-term retention while keeping recent logs available for frequent queries. What storage strategy fits?

answers.text: Keep all logs unpartitioned in one object forever
Delete recent logs immediately after ingestion
Use S3 lifecycle policies and partitioned layouts that align cost with access patterns
Move all current incident logs to offline storage before analysis

explanations.a: One unpartitioned object makes queries inefficient and operations difficult.
explanations.b: Immediate deletion removes the data analysts are most likely to query.
explanations.c: Lifecycle and partitioning can preserve logs for required periods while keeping analytics efficient and cost-aware.
explanations.d: Current incident logs need to remain accessible during response.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.3: Implement log storage and log data lakes and integrate with third-party security tools.
questions.keyword: Log storage and security data lake integration
questions.text: A security data lake receives duplicate data from multiple collectors. What should be implemented?

answers.text: Silently drop all events from one source without analysis
Treat every duplicate as a separate breach
Delete timestamps from duplicate events
Deduplication or source-priority logic that preserves traceability

explanations.a: Dropping a source can create detection gaps if it contains unique fields.
explanations.b: Duplicate telemetry can inflate incident counts and waste response effort.
explanations.c: Removing timestamps harms correlation and does not solve duplication.
explanations.d: Deduplication reduces repeated findings while preserving source information for audit and validation.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.3: Implement log storage and log data lakes and integrate with third-party security tools.
questions.keyword: Log storage and security data lake integration
questions.text: A centralized log lake must integrate with a third-party tool in another account. What sharing approach is appropriate?

answers.text: Grant narrowly scoped cross-account access to the required data through resource policies or service integration
Share the log archive account root credentials
Make all raw logs publicly readable
Email compressed logs manually after every incident

explanations.a: Third-party access should be limited to the needed datasets and auditable principal, not broad lake administration.
explanations.b: Root credential sharing is unsafe and unnecessary.
explanations.c: Public raw logs expose sensitive operational and security data.
explanations.d: Manual email transfer is delayed, incomplete, and hard to govern.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.3: Implement log storage and log data lakes and integrate with third-party security tools.
questions.keyword: Log storage and security data lake integration
questions.text: A security lake must retain forensic evidence but also comply with deletion requirements for certain log categories. What should be designed?

answers.text: Retain every log forever regardless of requirement
Retention classes and lifecycle policies based on log type, legal requirements, and investigation needs
Delete all logs after one day for simplicity
Let each analyst manually delete objects without review

explanations.a: Indefinite retention can violate data minimization requirements and increase cost.
explanations.b: Different data classes can require different retention and deletion behavior, so lifecycle design must be explicit.
explanations.c: Very short retention can break investigation and audit requirements.
explanations.d: Manual ad hoc deletion can destroy evidence and violate retention policy.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.3: Implement log storage and log data lakes and integrate with third-party security tools.
questions.keyword: Log storage and security data lake integration
questions.text: A security data lake receives logs from multiple Regions. What metadata is necessary for reliable analysis?

answers.text: Only the storage class of the log object
Only a random filename with no event context
Region, account, source service, event time, resource ID, and event type
Only the analyst who last queried the data

explanations.a: Storage class does not identify where or why the event occurred.
explanations.b: Random filenames make event filtering and ownership analysis difficult.
explanations.c: Consistent source metadata allows correlation and scoping across Regions and accounts.
explanations.d: Query user identity is useful for audit, but it does not describe the event source.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.4: Use AWS services to analyze logs.
questions.text: A security analyst needs to find all failed console logins for a specific IAM user over the last 24 hours. Which service is appropriate?

answers.text: Amazon EFS Lifecycle policies
AWS Backup Vault Lock
AWS CodeDeploy deployment history
CloudTrail Lake or CloudTrail logs queried with Athena

explanations.a: EFS lifecycle policies manage storage classes and do not query authentication events.
explanations.b: Vault Lock protects backups and does not analyze console login activity.
explanations.c: Deployment history does not show console login failures.
explanations.d: CloudTrail records sign-in and management events, and query services can filter by user and time range.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.4: Use AWS services to analyze logs.
questions.text: An incident responder needs to query application errors in CloudWatch Logs for one request ID. Which tool should be used?

answers.text: CloudWatch Logs Insights
AWS Certificate Manager
Amazon VPC route tables
Amazon Inspector SBOM export only

explanations.a: Logs Insights can query CloudWatch log groups and filter structured or text logs by request ID.
explanations.b: ACM manages certificates and does not query application log groups.
explanations.c: Route tables determine network paths and do not analyze application errors.
explanations.d: Inspector output does not query runtime application logs by request ID.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.4: Use AWS services to analyze logs.
questions.text: A security team stores CloudTrail logs in S3 and wants SQL-based investigation by eventName and sourceIPAddress. Which service fits?

answers.text: AWS WAF rate-based rules
Amazon Athena
Amazon Cognito user pools
AWS DataSync

explanations.a: WAF rules evaluate web requests and do not run SQL over S3 logs.
explanations.b: Athena can query structured logs stored in S3 with SQL when tables are defined correctly.
explanations.c: Cognito manages application identities and does not query CloudTrail objects in S3.
explanations.d: DataSync transfers data and does not provide SQL analysis.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.4: Use AWS services to analyze logs.
questions.text: Security Hub shows many critical findings. What analysis step helps prioritize response?

answers.text: Sort findings by title length only
Ignore all findings from nonproduction accounts
Group findings by severity, affected resource, account, exploitability, and compliance status
Close all findings older than one day automatically

explanations.a: Title length does not represent risk or urgency.
explanations.b: Nonproduction findings can still reveal systemic risk or exposed data.
explanations.c: Prioritization requires context about impact, affected assets, and whether findings are related or exploitable.
explanations.d: Age alone does not prove a finding is resolved or low risk.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.4: Use AWS services to analyze logs.
questions.text: An analyst needs to determine whether a suspicious IP connected to workloads and also appears in DNS queries. What analysis approach fits?

answers.text: Review only Lambda deployment artifacts
Query only ECR image tags
Check only IAM password policy settings
Correlate VPC Flow Logs with Route 53 Resolver query logs by time and source resource

explanations.a: Deployment artifacts do not show network or DNS activity.
explanations.b: Image tags do not reveal runtime IP and DNS behavior.
explanations.c: Password policy does not correlate network and DNS events.
explanations.d: Network and DNS correlation can reveal whether the same workload communicated with or resolved suspicious infrastructure.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.4: Use AWS services to analyze logs.
questions.text: A team needs visual analysis of security metrics from OpenSearch dashboards. Which service is relevant?

answers.text: Amazon OpenSearch Service
AWS Backup
Amazon SQS FIFO
AWS CloudHSM

explanations.a: OpenSearch can index and search logs and provide dashboards for security analytics.
explanations.b: Backup manages recovery points and does not provide log search dashboards.
explanations.c: SQS FIFO orders messages and does not visualize log analytics.
explanations.d: CloudHSM provides dedicated HSMs and not log dashboard analytics.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.4: Use AWS services to analyze logs.
questions.text: A Macie finding identifies sensitive data in a public bucket. What should the analyst validate?

answers.text: Only the bucket's display color in a dashboard
Bucket exposure, object classification, access history, and data owner
Only the number of Lambda aliases in the account
Only whether the bucket name is short

explanations.a: Display styling does not validate sensitive data exposure.
explanations.b: Macie findings need context about public accessibility, classification confidence, access, and ownership before remediation.
explanations.c: Lambda aliases do not describe S3 object sensitivity or exposure.
explanations.d: Bucket name length does not validate data sensitivity or access risk.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.4: Use AWS services to analyze logs.
questions.text: A query over S3 logs is slow and expensive. What data layout improvement can help?

answers.text: Combine all logs into one uncompressed file with no prefixes
Remove timestamps from every record
Partition logs by fields such as account, Region, service, and date
Encrypt the query text only

explanations.a: One unpartitioned file increases scan work and slows analysis.
explanations.b: Timestamps are essential for time-bounded investigations.
explanations.c: Partitioning reduces scanned data and improves performance for common investigation filters.
explanations.d: Encrypting query text does not reduce scanned log volume.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.5: Use AWS services to normalize, parse, and correlate logs.
questions.text: A company receives logs from multiple AWS services in different formats. The security team wants consistent searches for actor, source IP, resource, and action. What should be implemented?

answers.text: Keep every source format with unrelated field names and no mapping
Remove actor and source IP fields to simplify records
Store logs only as compressed screenshots
Log parsing and normalization into consistent field names

explanations.a: Unmapped formats make cross-source analysis slower and less reliable.
explanations.b: Removing key fields harms attribution and investigation.
explanations.c: Screenshots cannot be parsed into consistent fields for search.
explanations.d: Consistent fields allow analysts to query related concepts across heterogeneous log sources.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.5: Use AWS services to normalize, parse, and correlate logs.
questions.text: A pipeline enriches events before sending them to a SIEM. Which enrichment is useful for correlation?

answers.text: Account name, organizational unit, environment, application owner, and resource tags
Random emojis added to every event
Full plaintext secrets for each affected service
A new arbitrary field name for every event

explanations.a: Ownership and environment context helps correlate findings and route response across accounts.
explanations.b: Decorative fields do not support reliable investigation or routing.
explanations.c: Secrets should not be added to event records.
explanations.d: Inconsistent fields reduce correlation quality.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.5: Use AWS services to normalize, parse, and correlate logs.
questions.text: A team wants to correlate GuardDuty findings with CloudTrail activity. What field handling is important?

answers.text: Drop account IDs because all accounts are similar
Preserve resource identifiers, principal identifiers, event time, and account context
Round every event time to the nearest month
Hash every resource ID with a different salt per event

explanations.a: Account context is essential in multi-account investigations.
explanations.b: Correlation depends on stable identifiers and time windows that connect findings to audit events.
explanations.c: Coarse timestamps make incident timelines inaccurate.
explanations.d: Changing identifiers per event prevents reliable joining.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.5: Use AWS services to normalize, parse, and correlate logs.
questions.text: A log processor normalizes fields but fails when new services add optional fields. What design should be improved?

answers.text: Reject all events that include new fields
Overwrite raw events after parsing succeeds
Schema handling that tolerates optional and unknown fields while preserving raw events
Convert unknown fields into empty strings without record

explanations.a: Rejecting new fields can create ingestion gaps during service updates.
explanations.b: Keeping raw events supports reprocessing and audit when parsers change.
explanations.c: Security log pipelines should parse known fields without discarding unexpected data that may be useful later.
explanations.d: Discarding unknown data can remove investigation context.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.5: Use AWS services to normalize, parse, and correlate logs.
questions.text: An analyst needs to correlate CloudFront logs and AWS WAF logs for the same request. What should be preserved?

answers.text: Only the WAF rule description length
Only the CloudFront distribution comment
Only storage lifecycle transition date
Request identifiers, timestamps, client IPs, host, URI, and action fields

explanations.a: Description length does not connect a WAF decision to a CloudFront request.
explanations.b: Distribution comments do not identify individual requests.
explanations.c: Lifecycle dates do not correlate request logs.
explanations.d: Shared request context enables correlation between edge delivery and WAF decisions.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.5: Use AWS services to normalize, parse, and correlate logs.
questions.text: A central logging platform must send normalized alerts to third-party tools. What format consideration aligns with SCS-C03 topics?

answers.text: Use OCSF-compatible normalization where supported
Use a private one-off schema with no documentation for every source
Convert all findings to plain English only
Remove severity and category from all records

explanations.a: OCSF-compatible structure improves interoperability with tools that consume standardized cybersecurity events.
explanations.b: Undocumented source-specific schemas make integrations difficult.
explanations.c: Narrative text alone is harder for tools to parse and correlate.
explanations.d: Severity and category are important for routing and prioritization.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.5: Use AWS services to normalize, parse, and correlate logs.
questions.text: A log correlation workflow finds the same source IP in WAF blocks and successful login events. What should the workflow do?

answers.text: Automatically delete the successful login events
Link the events by IP, identity, time window, and request context for analyst review
Assume every matching IP is benign without review
Create unrelated resource tags instead of linking events

explanations.a: Deleting evidence prevents understanding whether account access was compromised.
explanations.b: Correlation should preserve enough context to determine whether the activity is suspicious or expected.
explanations.c: A match can be benign or malicious and needs context.
explanations.d: Tags alone do not establish an investigation relationship.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.6: Determine and configure appropriate log sources based on network design, threats, and attacks.
questions.text: A workload uses public ALB endpoints and private application subnets. The security team wants to detect blocked and allowed traffic at subnet boundaries. Which log source should be configured?

answers.text: Only CloudTrail management events
Only application debug logs
VPC Flow Logs for relevant subnets or network interfaces
Only CodeBuild reports

explanations.a: CloudTrail records API calls and does not show every network flow.
explanations.b: Application logs may not show traffic blocked before reaching the application.
explanations.c: VPC Flow Logs provide allowed and rejected network flow metadata for VPC resources.
explanations.d: Build reports do not capture runtime network flows.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.6: Determine and configure appropriate log sources based on network design, threats, and attacks.
questions.text: A company uses Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall to block known malicious domains. Which logs help evaluate DNS-based threats?

answers.text: EBS volume queue length metrics
CloudFormation template parameters only
S3 inventory reports only
Route 53 Resolver query logs and DNS Firewall logs or metrics where available

explanations.a: Storage metrics do not show queried domains or DNS firewall decisions.
explanations.b: Template inputs do not show runtime DNS queries.
explanations.c: Inventory reports describe objects and do not show DNS threat behavior.
explanations.d: DNS query and firewall telemetry show domain lookups and policy actions related to malicious domains.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.6: Determine and configure appropriate log sources based on network design, threats, and attacks.
questions.text: A transit gateway connects production VPCs, inspection VPCs, and on-premises networks. Which logging helps analyze traffic through the central hub?

answers.text: Transit gateway flow logs
Lambda function URL access logs only
IAM credential reports
CloudWatch dashboard widget labels

explanations.a: Transit gateway flow logs provide visibility into traffic traversing the transit gateway attachments.
explanations.b: Function URL logs do not show network flows through a transit gateway.
explanations.c: Credential reports describe IAM users and not network traffic through the hub.
explanations.d: Widget labels do not collect traffic metadata.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.6: Determine and configure appropriate log sources based on network design, threats, and attacks.
questions.text: A security engineer wants to detect possible data exfiltration from an EC2 instance to an unusual external IP. Which signals should be combined?

answers.text: Only the AMI creation timestamp
VPC Flow Logs, DNS query logs, GuardDuty findings, and application logs
Only the number of CloudWatch alarms
Only the length of the instance name tag

explanations.a: AMI age does not show outbound traffic behavior.
explanations.b: Exfiltration investigation benefits from network flows, domain resolution, threat detection, and workload context.
explanations.c: Alarm count does not reveal data movement to an external IP.
explanations.d: Tag length has no exfiltration detection value.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.6: Determine and configure appropriate log sources based on network design, threats, and attacks.
questions.text: A CloudFront distribution receives requests with suspicious user agents and high request rates. Which sources should be enabled?

answers.text: Only RDS slow query logs
Only EFS lifecycle events
CloudFront access logs and AWS WAF logs
Only AWS Backup job logs

explanations.a: Database slow queries do not capture edge request user agents.
explanations.b: EFS lifecycle activity does not show CloudFront web attack traffic.
explanations.c: Edge access and WAF logs show viewer request characteristics, rate-limit actions, and rule matches.
explanations.d: Backup job logs do not show edge request patterns.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.6: Determine and configure appropriate log sources based on network design, threats, and attacks.
questions.text: A hybrid connection over Site-to-Site VPN experiences suspicious traffic from on-premises. What should be collected for security analysis?

answers.text: Only Lambda cold start metrics
Only S3 object lock retention mode
Only application release notes
VPC Flow Logs, transit gateway flow logs if used, and firewall or VPN-adjacent logs

explanations.a: Cold start metrics do not describe hybrid network traffic.
explanations.b: Object retention does not show VPN traffic sources.
explanations.c: Release notes do not provide traffic evidence.
explanations.d: Hybrid traffic investigation needs network metadata at the VPC and transit layers plus security controls on the path.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.2.6: Determine and configure appropriate log sources based on network design, threats, and attacks.
questions.text: A public S3 bucket serves static content and uses CORS. Suspicious cross-origin requests are reported. What should be logged or reviewed?

answers.text: S3 server access or CloudTrail data events, CloudFront logs if used, and bucket CORS configuration
Only EC2 instance memory metrics
Only DynamoDB stream records
Only ECR image scan findings

explanations.a: CORS-related investigation needs object access evidence, edge request context where applicable, and the actual CORS rules.
explanations.b: Memory metrics do not show S3 object access or CORS rules.
explanations.c: DynamoDB streams do not show S3 cross-origin object access.
explanations.d: Image findings do not explain S3 CORS behavior.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.3.1: Analyze the functionality, permissions, and configuration of resources.
questions.text: A Lambda function should log security validation failures, but no log stream is created. What should be checked?

answers.text: Only the function's reserved concurrency setting
Execution role logs permissions and whether the function emits log output
Only the VPC route table for a public subnet
Only the S3 lifecycle policy for deployment artifacts

explanations.a: Concurrency limits do not create log streams or grant log permissions.
explanations.b: Lambda logging requires both log write permissions and runtime log statements or errors.
explanations.c: Route tables do not grant CloudWatch Logs permissions.
explanations.d: Artifact lifecycle does not control Lambda log delivery.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.3.1: Analyze the functionality, permissions, and configuration of resources.
questions.text: API Gateway access logging is enabled, but the execution role lacks permission to write to CloudWatch Logs. What failure is likely?

answers.text: The API automatically becomes private
All Lambda authorizers stop evaluating tokens
Access logs do not appear or logging delivery fails
S3 object encryption is disabled

explanations.a: Logging permissions do not change endpoint exposure.
explanations.b: Authorizer execution is separate from access log delivery.
explanations.c: API Gateway must be authorized to deliver logs to the configured CloudWatch Logs destination.
explanations.d: API Gateway log permissions do not control S3 encryption settings.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.3.1: Analyze the functionality, permissions, and configuration of resources.
questions.text: A CloudWatch agent configuration was updated to collect /var/log/secure, but no events are sent. What should be reviewed?

answers.text: Only CloudFront cache key settings
Only IAM Identity Center permission sets for human access
Only the EBS snapshot retention schedule
Agent status, configuration path, file permissions, and instance role permissions

explanations.a: Cache settings do not affect an EC2 log collection agent.
explanations.b: Human federation assignments do not make the agent read local files.
explanations.c: Snapshot retention does not ship log files.
explanations.d: The agent must be running with a valid config, able to read the file, and allowed to publish logs.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.3.1: Analyze the functionality, permissions, and configuration of resources.
questions.text: A health check alarm never changes state because the metric has no recent datapoints. What should be analyzed?

answers.text: Metric namespace, dimensions, period, and whether the monitored resource publishes the metric
Only the alarm description grammar
Only the account alternate contact
Only the ACM certificate validation method

explanations.a: Missing datapoints often come from incorrect metric identity or a resource that is not emitting the expected signal.
explanations.b: Description wording does not publish datapoints.
explanations.c: Contact information does not affect metric emission.
explanations.d: Certificate validation does not publish the unrelated health metric.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.3.1: Analyze the functionality, permissions, and configuration of resources.
questions.text: A CloudFront distribution is configured for logging but no logs arrive in the destination bucket. What should be checked?

answers.text: Only the Lambda function timeout
Supported logging destination, bucket ownership or permissions, and delivery configuration
Only the VPC subnet route table
Only the DynamoDB table partition key

explanations.a: Lambda timeout does not control CloudFront log delivery.
explanations.b: CloudFront logging depends on a valid destination and permissions for log delivery.
explanations.c: CloudFront is an edge service and log delivery is not controlled by workload subnet routes.
explanations.d: DynamoDB keys do not affect CloudFront access logs.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.3.1: Analyze the functionality, permissions, and configuration of resources.
questions.text: Security Hub is not showing findings from Inspector in one account. What should be analyzed?

answers.text: Only the workload's CPU reservation
Only the CloudWatch dashboard refresh interval
Inspector enablement, Security Hub integration, account membership, Region, and permissions
Only the EFS throughput mode

explanations.a: CPU reservation does not determine Security Hub finding ingestion.
explanations.b: Refresh interval does not enable Security Hub integrations.
explanations.c: Findings require the source service, aggregation path, and target Region/account integration to be configured.
explanations.d: EFS throughput does not control Inspector-to-Security Hub findings.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.3.1: Analyze the functionality, permissions, and configuration of resources.
questions.text: A VPC Flow Logs configuration exists, but analysts see no records for a new subnet. What should be checked?

answers.text: Only the subnet's Name tag spelling
Only the S3 object lock retention on unrelated logs
Only the number of EC2 key pairs
Flow log scope, subnet association, delivery destination, IAM role or resource policy, and traffic presence

explanations.a: A tag can help identify the subnet but does not attach or deliver flow logs by itself.
explanations.b: Object Lock does not attach flow logs to a subnet.
explanations.c: Key pair count has no effect on flow log delivery.
explanations.d: Flow logs must be attached to the right scope, have a valid delivery path, and receive traffic to produce records.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.3.2: Remediate misconfiguration of resources.
questions.text: The CloudWatch agent is installed on EC2 instances, but memory metrics are missing. What remediation should be applied?

answers.text: Update the agent configuration to collect memory metrics and restart or reload the agent
Enable S3 Versioning on an unrelated bucket
Change the ALB listener port
Rotate the instance key pair

explanations.a: The agent publishes only the metrics defined in its configuration, so the missing collection rule must be added and applied.
explanations.b: S3 Versioning does not add host memory metrics.
explanations.c: Listener ports do not control CloudWatch agent metric collection.
explanations.d: Key pair rotation does not enable memory metric publishing.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.3.2: Remediate misconfiguration of resources.
questions.text: API Gateway logs are missing because the account-level CloudWatch Logs role is not configured. What should be remediated?

answers.text: Increase Lambda memory for every backend function
Configure the API Gateway CloudWatch Logs role and stage logging settings
Delete the API stage and recreate it manually without logging
Change the DNS TTL for the API domain

explanations.a: Function memory does not fix API Gateway log delivery permissions.
explanations.b: API Gateway needs the required logging role and stage configuration before it can deliver logs.
explanations.c: Recreating without logging leaves the same detection gap.
explanations.d: DNS TTL does not grant log delivery permissions.

questions.name: Detection
questions.objective: Skill 1.3.2: Remediate misconfiguration of resources.
questions.text: CloudTrail was accidentally disabled in a workload account. What remediation is appropriate?

answers.text: Ignore the gap if no application errors occurred
Delete prior CloudTrail logs to reset the state
Re-enable the trail or organization trail delivery and investigate who disabled it
Replace CloudTrail permanently with CPU metrics

explanations.a: Audit logging gaps matter even when applications appear healthy.
explanations.b: Deleting audit history destroys evidence.
explanations.c: Audit logging should be restored quickly, and the disabling event must be investigated as a security-relevant action.
